explanation: Compared against erdosproblems.com/887 (Erdős–Rosenfeld): is there an absolute K such that for every C > 0 and all large n, n has at most K divisors in (n^{1/2}, n^{1/2} + C n^{1/4})? The Lean statement ∃ K ∀ C > 0, eventually, #{d ∈ Ioo ⌊√n⌋ ⌈√n + C n^{1/4}⌉ | d ∣ n} ≤ K. For integers d, ⌊√n⌋ < d ⟺ √n < d and d < ⌈x⌉ ⟺ d < x, so the natural-number interval is exactly the open real interval. Faithful.
